faqs.question: Heavy coated or thick paper does not load correctly or loads skewed. What should I do?
faqs.answer: The paper you are using may be too heavy or glossy for the paper roller to pick up. Be sure the paper is within printer specifications.

faqs.question: I am unable to connect my product to a wireless network. What should I do?
faqs.answer: The printer does not come with built-in wireless features and does not support a wireless (or Ethernet) connection to a network router. Only a direct wired connection to the computer is supported.

faqs.question: Does Epson have a program where I can donate my working electronic equipment?
faqs.answer:
Yes. Epson America, Inc. and
Digitunity

faqs.question: Does OS X support manual duplex printing with my product?
faqs.answer: This feature is not supported in Mac OS X. However, if your printer has a built-in automatic duplexer, auto-duplexing is supported in Mac OS X 10.6 (Snow Leopard).

faqs.question: How do I change the font size of text when I print from software in Windows?
faqs.answer: You need to select the text or font size in the software you are printing from, not the printer driver. For detailed instructions, contact the company for the application you are printing from.

faqs.question: Calibration doesn't seem to have any effect. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Make sure that whenever you turn off the printer, you are always using the printer's power button. Never use an external switch, such as a power strip, surge protector, or power protector, to turn off the printer. If you turn the printer off using an external switch, calibration settings will not be saved.

faqs.question: Are the ink cartridges refillable?
faqs.answer: EPSON does not recommend refilling ink cartridges. Refilled cartridges can cause print quality problems. In the printer's User's Guide, we advise "Use only genuine EPSON ink cartridges and do not refill them. Other products may cause damage not covered by EPSON's warranty".

faqs.question: I have just installed the ink cartridges and the ink out light stays on. How can I clear my product?
faqs.answer: Make sure the yellow tape is removed from the top of each cartridge and that the cartridges are correctly installed; follow the procedure for replacing the ink cartridges in the Reference Guide. Turn the printer off and back on. If the condition persists, follow the procedures for replacing the ink cartridges and lift the print head locking lever and snap it down firmly to ensure that you have broken the new seal. You should hear a good solid click. If you continue to have difficulties, the printer may need to go in for service. If the printer is within the dealers exchange period, have the printer exchanged.

faqs.question: My product is not producing any black ink. How can I resolve this problem?
faqs.answer: Using the inside front cover of the printer as a guide, perform two cleaning cycles on the offending printhead; (BLACK Cleaning)-Press PAUSE button, then ALT and Economy/Condensed. Try printing again. If the problem persists, try another two cleaning cycles, and try printing again. If this did not resolve the problem have the printer sent in for repair.

faqs.question: How do I install the ink cartridge?
faqs.answer: Use the inside front cover of the printer as a reference. Press pause, press and hold ALT for five seconds. Remove the yellow tape seal from the top of each ink cartridge and insert it into the printer. Press the locking clamp down firmly, you should hear a good solid click. Press the ALT button, when the pause light stops flashing the printer is ready. In either case, initial installation or replacement, snap the locking clamp down firmly to ensure the inner seal is broken. The Setup Guide pages 1-5 through 1-9 has a detailed step-by-step procedure including diagrams for installing the ink cartridges. If you continue to have difficulties after reading and following the procedure, call the EPSON Connection Technical Support group for further assistance.

faqs.question: What is the correct way to load transparency paper?
faqs.answer: Load the Epson transparency sheet ensuring that the notch is at the top left of the sheet. The Stylus Color II "Reference Manual" outlines the procedure.

faqs.question: Can I use sheet labels with my product?
faqs.answer: The printer is capable of printing sheet labels designed specifically for ink jet printers. To avoid paper jams, manually load sheet labels into the printer, one sheet at a time.

faqs.question: My product doesn't feed paper correctly. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Here are a few suggestions to try:
You can try using the Epson cleaning sheet (has a sticky side) to pick up any excess paper residue. It's available from the Epson Store.
Try loading heavier stock paper, such as 24 lb. paper, if you haven't done so already.
Make sure there is 1/16 to 1/32 inch space on each side of the paper in the paper tray.
Move the paper type selector back and forth 5 times, to make sure it is not stuck.
Feed the tray with a minimum of 20 sheets of paper and try to see if it loads paper through.
The paper thickness lever has two settings, one for plain paper, (thin paper 20# to 24#) and one for envelopes and thick paper.
It should be on the 0 setting for thin paper and on the + setting for thick paper and envelopes.
The paper adjustment lever may be adjusted in between the two settings to accommodate paper that is not standard or that the operating/environmental conditions have changed.
Make sure the paper is loaded far enough into the printer to ensure good contact between the paper and the paper feed mechanism.
Reload the paper
If the printer continues to feed too many sheets, the paper may be sticking together (due to humidity)For testing purposes, try the following:
1. Place 20-30 sheets of paper in a microwave oven for 3/4 seconds on the medium setting (to dry the paper)
2. Fan the paper, separating each sheet to ensure that the paper is not sticking together.
3. Reload the paper into the printer.
4. Test print your document.
If all else fails change the brand or type of paper used, the paper specifications are located in the printer's user's manual.

faqs.question: The output I am getting from my is unacceptable. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Make sure the economy light on the printer is not on, and if printing on Epson special coated paper, check to ensure that the you are printing on the coated side of the paper. If the Economy light is on, press the Economy/Condensed button multiple times until the Economy/Condensed lights are both off. Press the Print Mode button until the two Print Mode lights are off. Economy mode is only intended for printing rough drafts and should not be enabled for normal print. Try printing again. If printing has not improved, perform a cleaning cycle (COLOR Cleaning)-Press the PAUSE button, then ALT and Print Mode, or (BLACK Cleaning)-Press the PAUSE button, then ALT and Economy/Condensed. Print the demo page to see if printing has improved (Power on the printer while holding down the ALT button for 10 seconds or until data light comes on or paper loads). If the quality is acceptable, verify that the correct driver is selected as the default driver. Make sure that COLOR is selected in the driver. Ensure that HALFTONING is NOT selected in the driver. Manipulate the Stylus driver settings. You may also want to manipulate the settings within the application to achieve the optimum print results. If the quality from the demo page is not acceptable, check the type of paper being used. The EPSON special coated paper which is specifically made for the Stylus inkjet series printers, delivers the best printed output. If the problem persists, replace the ink cartridge. The trouble shooting guide located in chapter six of the Users Manual provides additional information. If the print quality is still unacceptable, have the printer sent in for repair.

faqs.question: My printout has incorrect margins. What should I do?
faqs.answer: The paper may be loaded incorrectly. Make sure that the left and right edge guides are flush against both sides of the paper. Make sure the margins are set correctly in your software application (margins are not adjustable via the printer driver), and make sure you are not trying to print outside of the printable area of the page for your paper size (printable area of the page specifications are available in the User's Manual). Make sure the correct paper size is selected in the printer driver settings.

faqs.question: I am not getting either black or color on the demo page. What should I do?
faqs.answer: If this is a new installation or if the cartridges have been recently replaced, follow the procedure for replacing the ink cartridges and try lifting the print head locking lever and snapping it down firmly to ensure that you have broken the cartridge seal. You should hear a good solid click. Try running the demo page again. Perform two cleaning cycles; (COLOR Cleaning)-Press the PAUSE button, then ALT and Print Mode, or (BLACK Cleaning)-Press the PAUSE button, then ALT and Economy/Condensed. If this does not correct the problem, the printer may need to go in for service. If the printer is within the dealers exchange period, have the printer exchanged.

faqs.question: My printout has lines running through it. What should I do?
faqs.answer: This phenomena is called banding and may be caused by a clogged nozzle. Print the demo page by pressing the ALT button while applying power to the printer. Check to see if white lines appear through your text. If the white lines are present, perform two cleaning cycles; (COLOR Cleaning)-Press the PAUSE button, then ALT and Print Mode, or (BLACK Cleaning)-Press the PAUSE button, then ALT and Economy/Condensed. If the cleaning cycles do not correct the problem, print the default settings (Press Economy/Condensed and power the printer on) to ensure that "Autoline Feed" is off. If the condition persists, have the printer sent in for service. The trouble shooting guide located in chapter six of the Users Manual provides additional information.

faqs.question: One of my colors is missing. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Calibrate colors in the driver setup to the specific application or image. Set to Default and adjust from there. Perform self test (Press Load/Eject and power printer on) and check that seven colors are produced. If seven colors are not produced, perform default set mode (Press Economy/Condensed and power printer on) to inspect dots. If test print shows missing dots, perform two cleaning cycles; (COLOR Cleaning)-Press the PAUSE Button, then, Alt and Print Mode 'OR' (BLACK Cleaning) Press the PAUSE, then, Alt and Economy/Condensed. Run the self test again to see if printing has improved (Power on the Printer while holding down the Load/Eject-Button. If the self test is still missing one of the four colors, try replacing the ink cartridge. If the condition persists, have the printer sent in for repair.

faqs.question: My text looks dark gray. How can I get my product to print my text a truer black?
faqs.answer: Make sure the economy light on the printer is not on. This will ensure that the economy mode option is not selected. Perform a black cleaning cycle; (BLACK Cleaning)-Press the PAUSE button, then ALT and Economy/Condensed. Run the print demo to see if printing has improved (Power on the Printer while holding down the ALT-Button). If this does not correct the problem, replace the black ink cartridge. If the black text on the demonstration page is acceptable, the problem may be a setting in the printer driver. The monochrome setting in the driver will produce a truer black than the color setting. Enabling "MicroWeave" and "disabling ink density correction" within the Stylus COLOR II printer will also give a darker truer black output.

faqs.question: My print looks wavy or stair steps. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Print the demo page to ensure the printer is operating properly. If the print is normal, try moving the printer to another computer to eliminate the possibility of a defective printer cable, parallel port or software problem. If the problem persists, try recalibrating the printer with the Calibrat.exe utility program. Try printing again. If the problem persists, the printer may need to go in for service.

faqs.question: My printout is blurry or smeared. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Try cleaning the plastic output guide inside the printer with a soft dry cloth. If the problem persists, take the printer to an Epson Authorized Service Center.

faqs.question: Why won't the print spool manager start?
faqs.answer:
1. Delete the printer driver - go to Control Panel/Printers, highlight Stylus Color II, click Remove, and Yes.
2. Delete the spool manager's .INI file - go to either the MS-DOS Prompt or File Manager and delete the file EPSPMGR2.INI from the C:\Windows directory.
3. Reinstall the driver - Insert Epson driver disk, go to Program Manager, click File, Run, type A:\SETUP in the Command Line, and OK.
4. Once the driver is reinstalled, follow the steps below on setting up the spool manager:
Go to Control Panel/Printers, and make sure the Stylus Color II is set as the default printer.
Disable "Use Print Manager" (it should be unmarked).
Click on Connect, make sure the correct port is selected (most likely LPT1: Local Port), disable "Fast Printing Direct to Port" then click OK.
Close out of Control Panel.
Go to MS-DOS prompt and create a unique spool directory on the root of the C:\ drive (type MD SPOOL).
Open Epson Spool Manager. If you don't have the icon for it, go to Program Manager, click File, Run, and in the Command Line type EPSPMGR2.
Make sure the Stylus Color II is highlighted, click Options, Default Spool Directory, change directory to C:\SPOOL and click OK.
Click Queue, Setup, verify that Spool Directory is C:\SPOOL and that "Spool to local printer" and "Use Print Manager for this port" are selected (both should be marked).
Close out Queue Setup and Epson Spool Manager then try printing again.

faqs.question: My product's control panel locks up after I print a document from Windows. The buttons on the panel do not respond unless I disconnect the parallel cable from the back of my product. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Some computers send an initialize/reset signal during the boot-up process. If the printer cable picks up any noise during this process, the initialize line will not complete its reset phase and cause the control panel to lock. Try booting the computer to Windows, then turn the printer ON using the printer's power switch and try printing again. A defective cable can also cause this situation. Make sure you are using a fully-shielded parallel cable, preferably 6 feet or less.

faqs.question: Why won't my product do a self test?
faqs.answer: Verify that the correct procedure for printing the self test has been performed. This problem is commonly caused by not holding down the required button long enough. Power on the printer while holding down the ALT button until the data light comes on and the printer starts to load the paper. If the printhead is moving back and forth but there is no ink on the page, press pause, then turn the printer off. Perform two cleaning cycles; (COLOR Cleaning)-Press the PAUSE button, then ALT and Print Mode, or (BLACK Cleaning)-Press the PAUSE button, then ALT and Economy/Condensed. Try performing the self test again. If self test still shows no ink on the page, ensure that the ink cartridges have been properly installed. Follow the procedures for replacing the ink cartridges and try lifting the print head locking lever and snapping it down firmly to ensure that you have broken the cartridge seal. You should hear a good solid click. Try the self test again. If the problem persists, contact the place of purchase for an exchange or have the printer sent in to be serviced.

faqs.question: My product is severely malfunctioning (no power, loud noises). What should I do?
faqs.answer: Remove the printer cable from the printer and verify the power source. Make sure that all packing material has been removed (head lock transportation key, etc.). Power the printer off and back on and perform the reset function on the printer. If the problem persists, take the printer to an Epson Authorized Service Center.
